analysis.title: Dick's Sporting Goods (DKS): Promotional breadth and depth at Foot Locker increase sequentially
key_insights: GS store checks at Foot Locker on 11/16/26 in NYC (Union Square legacy store and Fast Break location) found a significant increase in promotional breadth and a modest increase in promotional depth versus the 10/29 check.

Approximate share of the legacy store's sections on promotion was 44%, versus 29% on 10/29, a historical average of 25%, and 37% at a Jersey City check on 11/13/25. Average promotion was 29%, versus 28% on 10/29 and a 25% historical average.
The increase in promotional breadth was visible across all brands. New Balance saw the largest increase, with about 68% of styles on promotion versus about 41% on 10/29.
A new clearance table in the main section of the legacy store featured only Nike footwear (Jordans, Nike Air, Dunk Lows) at $69.99. The Kids section clearance table remained in place.
At the Fast Break location, GS continued to see markdowns across Nike, New Balance and Hoka, minimal Adidas discounts in women's, and fewer markdowns in men's.
A 11/3 check at Going, Going, Gone! showed increased footwear inventory versus prior visits.
GS says industry promotions have risen but do not change DKS's competitive positioning or its ability to take share, citing strong vendor relationships.

At 2Q earnings management lowered the FY26 Dick's business operating margin guide to 10.6-10.9% (about $70mn lower at the midpoint) and the Foot Locker operating margin guide to -1.1% to -0.5% (about $190mn lower at the midpoint). GS thinks guidance has been lowered enough to reflect industry pressure.
Management is in active talks with vendors for support on markdown dollars, which GS sees as a possible source of upside.
GS sees a path for innovative designs to resonate as the industry clears slower-moving legacy silhouettes, and says Dick's will have access to them.
Buy rating with a 12-month price target of $170 against a $136.14 price (24.9% upside). DKS is down 28.8% over 3 months and 34.2% over 12 months on an absolute basis.

market_movers.rationale: Guidance has been lowered enough to reflect industry pressure, and vendor markdown support could be upside. Foot Locker promotions rose sequentially, but GS does not see Dick's competitive positioning changing.

earnings_insights: Management lowered the FY26 Dick's business operating margin guide to 10.6-10.9% at 2Q earnings, about $70mn lower at the midpoint.
Management lowered the FY26 Foot Locker operating margin guide to -1.1% to -0.5% at 2Q earnings, about $190mn lower at the midpoint.

GS estimates, diluted EPS pre-exceptionals: FY1/27E $11.58, FY1/28E $15.12, FY1/29E $19.08, versus $13.20 for FY1/26 (reported basis per GS tables). Quarterly: 7/26 $3.53, 10/26E $1.81, 1/27E $3.34, 4/27E $3.54.
GS estimates revenue of $22,192mn for FY1/27E (+28.9%), $23,291mn for FY1/28E and $24,576mn for FY1/29E.
risk_factors: A weaker demand environment amid economic uncertainty.
Delays in improving the Foot Locker business.
Potential for inventory overhang and discounting in the industry.
charts_described: Exhibit 2 shows Foot Locker promotional breadth increasing sequentially from Feb-26 to Nov-26 and reaching a level higher than all previous checks.
Exhibit 3 shows Foot Locker promotional depth increasing sequentially and now above the historical average.

tension_points.theme: Foot Locker promotions and DKS positioning
tension_points.bull_case: Guidance already cut (Dick's margin guide about $70mn lower, Foot Locker about $190mn lower), vendor markdown support is under discussion, and strong vendor relationships protect Dick's share.
tension_points.bear_case: Promotional breadth at Foot Locker is at its highest of all checks (44%) and depth is above the historical average. Footwear inventory is rising at Going, Going, Gone!, which points to industry discounting and inventory overhang.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further inventory overhang and discounting in the industry, or delays in improving the Foot Locker business, per GS's stated downside risks.

theme_stances.key_argument: Industry promotions have risen but do not change Dick's competitive positioning given its strong vendor relationships.
theme_stances.evidence: we do not believe this changes Dick's competitive positioning
